component.title: Papyrus
component.description: Papyrus is a single-tenant agent runtime that an organization deploys in its own environment as a hardened container image or an Azure VM appliance. It runs model-driven agents and workflows over the organization's documents and connected systems, authenticates people with Microsoft Entra ID, and routes consequential external actions through human approval and an append-only ledger. Deployments created through Beag Labs call an external control plane and license authority (papyrus.beaglabs.com, license.beaglabs.com) outbound only; those services are outside this repository and outside the scope of this file.

controls.title: Account Management
controls.statement: Papyrus creates no local user accounts or passwords; every person is a Microsoft Entra identity (tenant ID and object ID) and authority comes only from the eleven declared Papyrus roles. On deployments that sign in through Beag Labs, roles live in a Papyrus role-assignment table: the consenting admin is seeded as the first System Owner, only a System Owner (never an API key) can grant or revoke roles, the last System Owner cannot be revoked, and every grant and revocation is written to an append-only event table protected by database triggers. Automation uses API keys, which are service identities with no roles that name the workflows they may run, expire after 1 to 365 days (default 90), and can be rotated or revoked with creation, rotation, revocation and last use recorded.
controls.customer: Own the account lifecycle in Entra ID: identity proofing, approval of app-role assignments, periodic access review, disabling departed users, and guest policy. Review Papyrus role assignments and API keys on the organization's review cadence.

controls.title: Access Enforcement
controls.statement: Every protected HTTP route authenticates the caller server-side and rejects principals that hold no Papyrus role; administrative, integration, approval, audit and owner-only operations check the specific role on the server before acting. MCP servers, imported APIs, Resource Classes and API keys are scoped to the caller's tenant, and an API key is admitted only to start runs of the workflows it names and read the runs it started. Sensitive Resource Class fields are masked except for administrators and the Class's sensitive-reader groups.
controls.customer: Assign Papyrus roles in Entra (or on the Access page for brokered deployments) according to organizational need-to-know.

gap.description: Agent sessions, their messages, the AgentFS Library and generated artifacts are owned by the tenant, not by the person who created them. Any signed-in person holding any Papyrus role can list and read every session, Library file and artifact in the deployment.
gap.remediation: Record an owner on each session and Library namespace, enforce owner or explicit-share checks in the session, workspace-file and artifact routes, and add tests for cross-user denial.

controls.title: Information Flow Enforcement
controls.statement: Papyrus enforces several fixed flow rules in code: agent workspace commands run with network access denied (Factory sidecar commands do not; see sc-39); Hosted App frames carry connect-src 'none' and reach data only through brokered, operation-specific connector grants; credentials are resolved by trusted runtime code and never passed to models, App source or workspace processes; MCP tool results are labeled as external content and truncated at 64 KiB; and public intake can write only an endpoint's allow-listed fields and never person, group or reference fields. Outbound HTTP from workflows, MCP, imported APIs and Class endpoint sends must use HTTPS to a public address unless the host is explicitly listed as internal, may not embed credentials, and never follows redirects.
controls.customer: Set PAPYRUS_WORKFLOW_HTTP_DENYLIST and PAPYRUS_WORKFLOW_HTTP_INTERNAL_HOSTS to match the authorization boundary, and enforce egress policy at the network layer.

evidence.note: assertWorkflowHttpTarget: HTTPS, no URL credentials, denylist, refusal of non-public resolved addresses

gap.description: Outbound HTTP from workflow http-get/http-post steps and imported API tools is allowed to any public HTTPS host by default; the organization can block hosts with a denylist but there is no allow-list-only mode.
gap.remediation: Add an allow-list mode (deny by default) for workflow and imported-API egress, selectable per deployment profile and on by default for the government and disconnected profiles.

controls.title: Separation of Duties
controls.statement: The agent can propose but cannot approve: approveProposal, denyProposal and executeAction are rejected at the agent tool layer, and approval routes require a human Entra session holding Papyrus.Action.Approve. Workflow approval steps addressed to a person or group can be answered only by that person, a member of that group, or a System Owner, never by the person who started the run. Authority-weakening policy changes, non-additive Class changes and App publications wait for a Governance principal (System Owner, or Security.Manage plus Action.Approve).
controls.customer: Assign Papyrus.Action.Approve, Papyrus.Security.Manage and Papyrus.System.Owner to different people according to organizational separation-of-duties policy.

evidence.note: FORBIDDEN_AGENT_TOOLS lists approveProposal, denyProposal, executeAction

verification.note: Keeps approval and execution out of the agent's tools
Requester cannot approve their own addressed request, even as an approver

gap.description: Action proposals and governed changes do not check that the approver differs from the person who proposed or requested them, so one person holding the approving roles can approve their own request. Unaddressed workflow approval steps can be answered by the run's initiator.
gap.remediation: Refuse approval when the approver's object ID equals the proposer or requester for action proposals, governed changes and unaddressed workflow steps, with an explicit single-operator override recorded in the audit log.

controls.title: Least Privilege
controls.statement: Papyrus splits authority into roles (integration view and manage, security manage, action approve, audit view and system owner) and checks the narrowest one per operation; Papyrus.System.Owner implies all of them. API keys hold no roles. Customer agents receive only read tools for their configured Classes and run as the requesting person. The container runs as a non-root user, and workspace commands run with the data directory unreadable and network denied.
controls.customer: Grant the narrowest role that fits each person, limit System Owner assignments, and do not run the container privileged.

evidence.note: ENTRA_APP_ROLES and OBSERVABILITY_APP_ROLES

gap.description: Possession of any role, including narrow ones such as Papyrus.Audit.View, grants access to the shared agent workspace: all sessions, chat, Library files and artifacts. Workspace access is not itself a separately assignable privilege.
gap.remediation: Introduce a distinct workspace-use role or per-session ownership (see ac-3) so that narrow roles do not carry workspace access.

controls.title: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts
controls.statement: Papyrus accepts no passwords, so interactive logon attempts and lockout are handled by Microsoft Entra ID. For the one Papyrus-managed secret a member of the public can guess, Resource Class request links with a confirmation question lock permanently after five wrong answers. Invalid, expired, revoked and rotated API keys all receive the same 401 response.
controls.customer: Configure Entra smart lockout, Conditional Access and sign-in risk policies for the tenant.

evidence.note: MAX_FAILED_CHECKS = 5; request link status set to locked

verification.note: Request links lock after five wrong answers

controls.title: Session Termination
controls.statement: The portal session is an HMAC-signed cookie with a one-hour lifetime whose expiry is checked server-side; after it expires the person must sign in through Entra again. Sign-out clears the cookie. On brokered deployments roles are re-read from the assignment table on every request, so revoking a person's roles ends their access on the next request.
controls.customer: Set Entra token lifetimes and Conditional Access sign-in frequency; use boundary controls if faster revocation is required.

evidence.note: portalCookie Max-Age=3600 with signed exp; verifyPortalCookie rejects expired cookies; clearCookie
/api/auth/logout clears the cookie

verification.note: A revoked role ends at once on brokered deployments

gap.description: Sessions are stateless: there is no server-side session store, idle timeout, or revocation list. A copied cookie remains valid until its one-hour expiry after sign-out, and on deployments using their own app registration the roles carried in the cookie persist until expiry after an Entra role is removed.
gap.remediation: Add a server-side session table with idle timeout, explicit revocation on sign-out, and an administrator action to end a person's sessions.

controls.title: Event Logging
controls.statement: Papyrus records integration lifecycle events and action-ledger decisions (proposed, approved, denied, executed) in a hash-chained event table; role grants and revocations; every MCP tool call and MCP administrative change; API key creation, rotation and revocation; policy versions and policy denials; governed change requests and approvals; and agent traces and logs in a separate observability store.
controls.customer: Decide which additional events the organization requires and collect Entra sign-in logs from Microsoft.

gap.description: Successful and failed sign-ins and authorization denials (401/403) are not written to a local audit record. A successful sign-in is only sent as an analytics event to Beag Labs on registered deployments.
gap.remediation: Write sign-in success, sign-in failure and authorization-denied events to an append-only local audit table with actor, time, route and outcome.

controls.title: Content of Audit Records
controls.statement: Audit rows carry an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, the actor's Entra object ID, the action, the affected integration, tool or resource, and the outcome. MCP call records add session, workflow, tool classification, approval ID, duration and a SHA-256 of the arguments; write calls keep the approved arguments, while tokens and results are never stored. Configuration events exclude secret values.

controls.title: Protection of Audit Information
controls.statement: Audit tables are append-only at the database layer: SQLite triggers abort UPDATE and DELETE on integration events, model events, role assignment events, MCP admin events and settled MCP call records. Integration and action-ledger events are additionally SHA-256 hash-chained, and the chain can be recomputed to detect modification.
controls.customer: Restrict host and database-file access, protect backups, and copy audit records to independently controlled immutable storage.

evidence.note: No-update/no-delete triggers and verifyEventChain

gap.description: Triggers and the hash chain detect changes made through the application only; anyone with write access to the database file can rewrite them. Chain verification is not exposed through any API or run on a schedule, and logs other than integration and action events are not hash-chained.
gap.remediation: Expose chain verification to Audit Viewers, run it periodically, extend chaining to all audit tables, and anchor chain heads in external storage.

controls.title: Audit Record Generation
controls.statement: Audit records are generated server-side at the enforcement points themselves: the proposal approval and denial paths, the single MCP call path, role assignment changes, API key management and policy enforcement. controls.title: Baseline Configuration
controls.statement: Papyrus ships one Dockerfile that builds a Wolfi-based runtime image running as a non-root user with no browser engine, plus a DoD variant that defaults to the DoD Microsoft cloud and embeds the offline license authority key. The Azure Marketplace appliance is provisioned by script: the container listens only on 127.0.0.1 behind an nginx TLS edge. Three deployment profiles (commercial, government, disconnected) set runtime posture.
controls.customer: Document the approved deployment configuration: host OS, network, Entra registration, model endpoint, storage and the Papyrus image digest.

evidence.note: Build and runtime stages, nonroot user, dod target

gap.description: The baseline is not fully reproducible: base images are referenced by tag rather than digest, apk packages are not version-pinned, and several Python packages in the runtime image (pypdf, pypdfium2, reportlab, pillow) are unpinned.
gap.remediation: Pin base images by digest and pin apk and pip package versions, with an automated update process that opens reviewed changes.

controls.title: Configuration Change Control
controls.statement: In-application changes that weaken policy, alter Classes non-additively, or publish Apps become digest-checked governed changes that apply only after a Governance principal approves them, and an approval is refused if the change's digest or expected version no longer matches. Papyrus software updates are announced by exact image digest from an allowed repository and installed only when a System Owner applies them or within an owner-configured maintenance window.
controls.customer: Operate organizational change control for deployment configuration, infrastructure and when updates are applied.

evidence.note: propose/approve with digest and expected-version checks

controls.statement: Configuration endpoints require specific roles on the server: Integration.Manage for model gateways, MCP servers, imported APIs, package mirrors, browser and mainframe settings and branding; System Owner for role assignments, updates, license activation and skill approval; Governance for governed changes. Model API keys are accepted only over HTTPS from the portal origin.

controls.title: Configuration Settings
controls.statement: Configuration is validated at startup and fails closed: persistent mode requires an HTTPS public origin and an Entra tenant and client ID; the development identity is accepted only in local mode; unknown profiles, national clouds and sandbox backends are rejected; TLS certificate and key must be set together; and the former license-bypass setting is refused. Once an HTTPS origin is configured, Host and X-Forwarded-Host headers cannot change OAuth redirect URIs or cookies.

In Azure Government or other national clouds, set PAPYRUS_AZURE_MANAGEMENT_ENDPOINT, PAPYRUS_AZURE_MANAGEMENT_RESOURCE, PAPYRUS_AZURE_KEYVAULT_DNS_SUFFIX and PAPYRUS_AZURE_KEYVAULT_RESOURCE; they default to Azure commercial endpoints and are not derived from PAPYRUS_ENTRA_CLOUD.

controls.title: Least Functionality
controls.statement: The runtime image contains no browser engine. The Papyrus agent has no general shell: native programs run only through structured executors (Python, Pandoc, LibreOffice) with fixed executables. MCP has no stdio transport. The public scheduler CRUD surface is not exposed, and removed legacy connectors read back as retired and cannot be activated or executed. The Factory sidecar that builds Apps is a separate process with its own command sandbox (see sc-39).
controls.customer: Expose only ports 80/443 (and SSH if needed), and disable integrations and model endpoints the organization does not use.

controls.statement: Release images are signed with Cosign keyless signing in GitHub Actions. On the Azure Marketplace appliance the updater runs cosign verify against a pinned signer identity and issuer before pulling an update and installs nothing if verification fails; the Marketplace image pipeline verifies the signature and build provenance of the container digest before baking it.
controls.customer: On self-hosted deployments, verify the image signature and digest before deployment.

gap.description: Signature verification exists only on the Marketplace VM update and image-build paths; the shell updater has no automated test, and other deployment paths do not verify signatures in this repository. The Azure template (deploy/azure/main.bicep) references ghcr.io/beaglabs/papyrus:0.1.1 by tag, a different repository from the one CI publishes (ghcr.io/beaglabs/papyrus/papyrus). Two workflows (container.yml and container-multiarch.yml) sign images for the same repository while the updater trusts only the container.yml identity.
gap.remediation: Settle on one signing workflow and identity, reference images by digest from the published repository in every deployment template, add an automated test for the updater verification step, and document signature verification for every supported deployment path.

controls.title: System Backup
controls.statement: Papyrus keeps its state in the data directory (agent.db, mastra.db, jobs.db, observability.db, secrets.db and AgentFS) and documents which files must be backed up together and that the local master key must be backed up separately. It provides no backup tooling.
controls.customer: Back up the data directory consistently, store the master key and Key Vault recovery separately, and test restoration.

evidence.note: Lists the databases to back up and master key handling

controls.title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
controls.statement: People authenticate only through Microsoft Entra ID. Direct sign-in uses the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256), single-use state and a nonce; ID tokens are verified against the tenant's published keys for issuer, audience (client ID or api:// form), expiry, nonce and tenant ID, and discovery metadata with an unexpected issuer is rejected. Brokered sign-in redeems a one-time handle server-to-server and accepts only an assertion signed by a configured license authority key, addressed to this deployment, matching the pending login nonce and bound tenant, and unexpired. Multi-factor and PIV/CAC requirements are enforced by Entra, not by Papyrus.
controls.customer: Require MFA or phishing-resistant authentication through Entra Conditional Access. Brokered deployments trust Beag Labs' control plane to run the Microsoft sign-in; organizations that cannot accept that should use their own app registration.

evidence.note: startLogin, completeLogin, verifyEntraToken, completeBrokeredLogin

verification.note: Accepts only a fresh assertion signed for this deployment, tenant and login

controls.statement: API key secrets are 32 random bytes, shown once with cache-control no-store, and stored only as an HMAC-SHA-256 keyed with the deployment secret, so a copied database cannot be used to call the API. Keys expire, can be rotated (the old secret stops immediately) and revoked. Integration settings reject inline passwords, tokens and keys and store only credential references, and model API keys are accepted only over HTTPS from the portal origin. The pre-commit hook scans staged changes for private keys and common token formats.

controls.title: Incident Handling
controls.statement: Papyrus provides no incident handling capability or plan. Its audit and observability records are inputs to the deploying organization's process.
controls.customer: Maintain and exercise an incident response plan covering the Papyrus deployment, including revoking roles, API keys and connector credentials and preserving audit databases.

controls.title: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
controls.statement: Beag Labs does not currently run automated vulnerability scanning of dependencies, source code or container images in CI. The SBOMs described under cm-8 are available as scanning inputs.
controls.customer: Scan hosts, the deployed image and surrounding infrastructure with the organization's tools.

gap.remediation: Add image and dependency scanning (for example Grype or Trivy against the CycloneDX SBOM) and static analysis to CI, failing builds on critical findings, and enable automated dependency update pull requests.

controls.title: External System Services
controls.statement: Connected deployments call Beag Labs services outbound only: registration, signed deployment status, brokered sign-in, staff-directory Graph tokens, analytics, and on control-plane deployments hourly agent-execution usage reports to papyrus.beaglabs.com/api/deployments/usage. Status and identity responses are accepted only when signed by a configured license authority key and addressed to this deployment, and the control plane URL must be HTTPS. Registration is skipped for the disconnected profile or when PAPYRUS_BEAGLABS_REGISTRATION=0. Other outbound services the code can call are huggingface.co (embedding model download on first use unless PAPYRUS_EMBEDDING_DOWNLOAD=0), GitHub or GitLab from the Factory when configured, public package registries for skill and session installs unless PAPYRUS_PACKAGE_PUBLIC_REGISTRIES=false or the profile is disconnected, and Sentry only when a DSN is set (with sendDefaultPii disabled).
controls.customer: Assess Beag Labs as an external service provider, or use the disconnected profile or set PAPYRUS_BEAGLABS_REGISTRATION=0 to avoid it.

The control plane and license authority are not in this repository and are not covered by this assessment.

controls.title: Developer Testing and Evaluation
controls.statement: The repository has workspace-wide TypeScript type checking and a Vitest suite for the server covering identity, authorization, MCP, Resource Classes, secrets, sandboxing and approvals. CI runs type checking and a fixed subset of tests (Factory, scoped workflows, mainframe guardrails and offline evaluations), and a local pre-commit hook runs secret, contract and compliance-drift checks plus security-invariant tests when related files change.

gap.remediation: Run the full server test suite and pnpm compliance:check in CI on every pull request and make them required checks.

Refuses an oversized chat body

gap.description: Rate limits are in memory and keyed on the socket address; behind the appliance's nginx proxy every client shares one address, and the limiter clears all windows once it tracks 10,000 keys. The cap of 256 pending sign-ins can be exhausted by unauthenticated requests, blocking sign-in for up to 10 minutes.
gap.remediation: Key limits on a trusted forwarded client address, bound memory without clearing all windows, and rate-limit /api/auth/entra/login per client instead of a global cap.

controls.title: Boundary Protection
controls.statement: On the Marketplace appliance the container is published only on 127.0.0.1 and reached through nginx. Every outbound call made for MCP, OAuth discovery, workflows, imported APIs and Class endpoint sends passes one check: HTTPS, no embedded credentials, an organization denylist, and refusal of hosts that resolve to loopback, private or link-local addresses (including cloud metadata) unless listed as internal; redirects are not followed. Calls to the Beag Labs control plane are outbound only. Workspace commands have no network access.
controls.customer: Place the deployment behind the organization's firewalls and proxies, restrict inbound access to 443, and set the egress denylist and internal-host list.

evidence.note: assertWorkflowHttpTarget
mcpFetch applies the same check and redirect: manual
docker run -p 127.0.0.1:${PAPYRUS_PORT}; nginx proxy
Deployment vault created with publicNetworkAccess Enabled

verification.note: Address classification, denylist and internal-host rules
Refuses private addresses and plain HTTP to public hosts

gap.description: The address check resolves DNS separately from the connection that follows, so a host that changes its DNS answer between the two can reach an internal address. The deployment Key Vault is created with public network access enabled.
gap.remediation: Connect to the address that was checked (pinned lookup) for all outbound requests, and support private endpoints or firewall rules for the deployment Key Vault.

controls.title: Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity
controls.statement: Persistent mode refuses to start without an HTTPS public origin. The daemon can terminate TLS itself with a TLS 1.2 minimum, and the Marketplace appliance's nginx edge allows only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 and sends HSTS. Portal cookies are Secure under HTTPS. Outbound connections to MCP servers, workflows, imported APIs, Class endpoints and the control plane require HTTPS except for hosts the organization explicitly lists as internal.
controls.customer: Provide certificates, TLS termination and cipher policy that meet organizational requirements.

evidence.note: Persistent deployments require an HTTPS PAPYRUS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN
createHttpsServer with minVersion TLSv1.2
ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3 and HSTS
PAPYRUS_CONTROL_PLANE_URL must use HTTPS

verification.note: Rejects plain HTTP to non-internal hosts
Rejects non-HTTPS remote secret entry even with spoofed forwarding headers

controls.title: Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management
controls.statement: The local secrets master key must be a separately provisioned 32-byte file that is not group- or world-writable and is opened without following symlinks; the server never generates it. Where Azure Key Vault is configured, the portal secret, Entra client secret and model and provider keys are kept in a deployment Key Vault (RBAC mode, purge protection, 90-day soft delete) with only the VM's managed identity granted access, and each reader is limited to its own secret-name prefix. License authority public keys are supplied by configuration or baked into the DoD image.
controls.customer: Provision, back up and protect the master key and portal secret; manage Entra and TLS keys.

evidence.note: Master key checks
Core vault and purpose-prefix read guard
Vault properties and single role assignment
Connector credential key derived as SHA-256 of the portal secret

verification.note: Fails closed with missing, insecure or incorrect master keys
Each caller reads only its own secrets; references refused without an Azure identity

gap.description: There is no rotation or key-versioning support for the portal secret or the local master key. Encryption keys for connector credentials are derived with a single SHA-256 of the portal secret, so changing that secret makes stored values unreadable. The Key Vault uses the Standard (software-protected) tier.
gap.remediation: Introduce versioned data-encryption keys with a proper KDF, a re-encryption procedure for rotation, and an option for HSM-backed keys.

controls.title: Cryptographic Protection
controls.statement: Papyrus uses the Node.js crypto module (OpenSSL) for AES-256-GCM encryption of stored credentials, HMAC-SHA-256 for cookies, API key hashes and webhook signatures, SHA-256 hash chains, SHA-256 signature verification of license, status and identity documents, and TLS; JWTs are verified with the jose library. FIPS mode is not enabled anywhere in the repository or image.
controls.customer: Where FIPS 140 validated cryptography is required, run on a validated module and terminate TLS on validated infrastructure.

evidence.note: AES-256-GCM
verifyAuthoritySignature with sha256
HMAC-SHA-256 portal cookie; jose jwtVerify
Runtime installs Wolfi nodejs-24; no FIPS configuration

gap.description: Papyrus does not enable OpenSSL FIPS mode or a FIPS provider, and the image is not built on a FIPS 140 validated cryptographic module. Algorithms in use are FIPS-approved, but no validated module is claimed.
gap.remediation: Build a FIPS variant of the image on a FIPS 140-3 validated OpenSSL provider, enable FIPS mode at startup, fail startup if it is unavailable, and test that every code path works under it.

controls.title: Mobile Code
controls.statement: Agent-built Hosted App and Factory preview code runs in an opaque iframe sandboxed to allow-scripts only, with a CSP of default-src 'none', connect-src 'none', form-action 'none' and base-uri 'none', loaded through a one-use frame ticket. App source that performs direct browser networking or contains credential literals or ambient secrets is rejected before release. HTML and SVG artifacts are served as attachments with a sandbox CSP.
controls.customer: Optionally route a separate HTTPS App origin (PAPYRUS_APP_ORIGIN) as defense in depth.

evidence.note: Sandboxed frame CSP and nonce-checked message bridge

verification.note: Rejects ambient secrets, browser networking and credential literals

controls.title: Session Authenticity
controls.statement: The portal session cookie is HMAC-SHA-256 signed with the deployment secret, compared in constant time, and set HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure and with the __Host- prefix under HTTPS. OIDC state and nonce are random 32-byte values held server-side, single-use and expiring after 10 minutes; MCP OAuth sign-ins are likewise single-use, bound to the initiating person and checked against the discovered issuer. Once an HTTPS origin is configured, request headers cannot change the origin used for redirects or cookies.

evidence.note: portalCookie, verifyPortalCookie, pending login state

verification.note: Refuses a callback from another person, a reused state and a different issuer

controls.title: Protection of Information at Rest
controls.statement: Papyrus encrypts secrets at the application layer with AES-256-GCM and per-record associated data: model gateway keys in a separate 0600 secrets database under a separately provisioned master key; and connector, imported-API and MCP credentials bound to their owner. Where Azure Key Vault is configured, platform secrets are stored there and configuration files hold only references.
controls.customer: Encrypt the volume that holds the data directory and its backups, and manage those keys.

evidence.note: secrets.db encryption and file permissions
Owner-bound AES-256-GCM connector credentials
Key Vault storage of platform secrets

verification.note: Encrypted persistence, tamper rejection and cross-profile binding
Shared MCP token stored encrypted and never returned
bootstrap.json holds only references

gap.description: Agent sessions, Library documents, Resource Class records, audit logs and traces are stored in unencrypted SQLite and AgentFS files; their protection at rest depends entirely on volume encryption that Papyrus neither provides nor checks.
gap.remediation: Document volume encryption as a deployment requirement and verify it on supported deployment configurations, or add database-level encryption for the main data stores.

controls.title: Process Isolation
controls.statement: Commands the Papyrus agent runs in its workspace run in a separate worker process under landstrip (Landlock and seccomp on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS) with writes limited to a temporary materialized workspace, the Papyrus data directory unreadable and network denied. The worker validates and resolves the effective policy before starting the command and refuses to run if the write root, network restriction or data-directory denial is not in effect; unsupported platforms run no workspace commands. Credential-like environment variables are removed before the command starts.
controls.customer: Run on a Linux host with Landlock enabled and do not run the container privileged.

evidence.note: landstrip policy, validate/resolve checks, fail-closed exits

Read-confinement check of the resolved policy
Factory sidecar constructs a Mastra LocalSandbox with only an environment allow-list, no native isolation

verification.note: Fails closed without OS isolation; strips credential-like environment values; rejects cwd traversal
Reports landstrip isolation and refuses escaping working directories
Rejects snapshots that include daemon data or parent roots

gap.description: The Factory sidecar, enabled by default in the image (PAPYRUS_FACTORY_SIDECAR=1), runs commands for App builds in Mastra's LocalSandbox with no kernel isolation: only its environment is restricted to an allow-list. Those commands run as the same user as the daemon, can read files that user can read, including the Papyrus data directory, and have network access.
gap.remediation: Run Factory sidecar commands under the same landstrip policy as agent workspace commands (data directory denied, network denied or limited to package mirrors and source control), or disable the sidecar by default until that is in place.

controls.title: Flaw Remediation
controls.statement: Beag Labs publishes fixes as new signed images. A deployment learns of a release through an HMAC-signed, timestamped webhook with replay protection, and a System Owner applies it or allows it to apply within a maintenance window; the Marketplace updater verifies the image signature before installing.
controls.customer: Set patch windows, test updates and apply them within organizational timeframes.

evidence.note: verifyWebhook, announce, apply, maintenance window
Signature verification and install

verification.note: Signature over timestamp and body, replay refusal, window-limited auto-apply

gap.description: Beag Labs has no documented flaw remediation timeframes by severity, and no published security advisory or vulnerability disclosure process (no SECURITY.md).
gap.remediation: Publish a vulnerability disclosure policy and severity-based remediation SLAs, and announce fixed vulnerabilities in release notes.

controls.title: System Monitoring
controls.statement: Papyrus records agent traces and logs in a separate observability database readable by System Owners, Audit Viewers and Security Managers, writes structured JSON warnings to standard output, and can send errors to a customer-supplied Sentry DSN. The container health check verifies that the landstrip sandbox enforces its boundary; it does not check that the HTTP service is answering.
controls.customer: Collect container output and audit data into the organization's monitoring platform and alert on it.

controls.title: Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity
controls.statement: Releases are referenced by image digest and signature-verified before the Marketplace updater installs them. Hosted App publication approves an immutable, digest-checked build. Governed changes are re-hashed at approval and refused if the digest differs. The stored control-plane status is re-verified against its signature on every read, so editing the file cannot lift a suspension. Integration and action events are hash-chained.
controls.customer: Verify image digests and signatures on deployment paths other than the Marketplace appliance.

controls.title: Information Input Validation
controls.statement: Request bodies must be JSON objects under per-route byte limits; required strings are length-bounded; policy rules are validated against a fixed schema; public forms accept only allow-listed fields and bounded uploads of permitted types and cannot reference Library paths; outbound addresses are validated before use; and webhook payloads are signature-checked over the exact raw bytes.

controls.title: Error Handling
controls.statement: Errors are returned as JSON with a code and a per-request ID. Known error types map to specific status codes, sign-in error pages do not echo request input, the browser connection address is masked in error text, and imported-API credentials are redacted from errors.
controls.customer: Configure log handling so diagnostic output is not exposed beyond administrators.

gap.remediation: Return a generic message for unmapped errors and log the detail server-side under the request ID.

controls.title: Provenance
controls.statement: Container images built from main are signed with Cosign and receive a GitHub build provenance attestation. Dependencies are locked in pnpm-lock.yaml and installed with --frozen-lockfile in CI, and the pnpm version is pinned with a hash in packageManager.
controls.customer: Retain the image digests and attestations for deployed releases and verify them at intake.

gap.description: GitHub Actions are referenced by mutable version tags rather than commit SHAs, and base images and OS and Python packages in the Dockerfile are not pinned, so build inputs are not fully traceable.
gap.remediation: Pin all Actions to commit SHAs and pin image and package inputs (see cm-2), recording them in the provenance attestation.

programGaps.title: No third-party assessment or penetration test
programGaps.description: No 3PAO assessment, independent security assessment or penetration test of Papyrus has been performed. All statements in this file are derived from the source repository and its automated tests.
programGaps.remediation: Commission an independent penetration test of the application and appliance, then a 3PAO assessment against the target baseline, and track findings in the POA&M.

programGaps.title: Controls not verified in an authorized hosting environment
programGaps.description: Papyrus has not been deployed or assessed within a FedRAMP-authorized or DoD Impact Level authorized boundary, and holds no ATO. The DoD image variant only changes the default Microsoft cloud and embeds the offline license key.
programGaps.remediation: Deploy a reference instance in an authorized environment and verify each control there with a sponsoring agency.

programGaps.title: FIPS 140 validated cryptography not enabled
programGaps.description: No code, configuration or image in the repository enables OpenSSL FIPS mode or a FIPS provider. Papyrus uses FIPS-approved algorithms through Node.js crypto but does not run on a validated module.
programGaps.remediation: Produce a FIPS image variant on a FIPS 140-3 validated provider with FIPS mode enforced at startup (see sc-13).

programGaps.title: Vulnerability scanning and remediation SLAs not formalized
programGaps.description: CI performs no dependency, static or image vulnerability scanning; there are no severity-based remediation timeframes and no published vulnerability disclosure policy.
programGaps.remediation: Add scanning to CI (see ra-5), publish a disclosure policy, and adopt remediation SLAs such as those in the FedRAMP continuous monitoring guidance.

programGaps.title: Incident response and contingency planning owned by the deploying organization
programGaps.description: Papyrus ships no incident response plan, contingency plan, or backup tooling. Each deploying organization must cover Papyrus in its own IR and CP documentation, and Beag Labs has no published process for notifying customers of product security incidents.
programGaps.remediation: Publish customer-facing guidance for IR and backup/restore of a Papyrus deployment and a Beag Labs product security incident notification process.

programGaps.title: Security tests and compliance checks not enforced in CI
programGaps.description: CI runs type checking and a subset of tests; most security tests and the compliance drift check run only locally through a pre-commit hook that can be bypassed. The generated compliance/ssp.md states that these checks also run in CI.
programGaps.remediation: Run the full test suite and pnpm compliance:check as required CI checks, and correct the SSP text until they do (see sa-11).

programGaps.title: First-run setup is not authenticated
programGaps.description: Before identity is configured, the setup server accepts the Entra tenant and client configuration from any caller that can reach it, with no setup token, once Terms are accepted and an entitlement is present. HTTPS is required for this step only on verified Marketplace deployments in persistent mode; elsewhere setup can run over plain HTTP.
programGaps.remediation: Require a one-time setup token printed to the host console or delivered through the deployment channel, and require HTTPS for setup in persistent mode on every deployment path.

programGaps.title: Beag Labs control plane and license authority outside assessment scope
programGaps.description: Control-plane deployments trust papyrus.beaglabs.com and license.beaglabs.com to entitle and suspend them, bind their tenant and first System Owner, broker Microsoft sign-in, and issue Graph tokens. That code is not in this repository and none of its controls are documented here.
programGaps.remediation: Produce a separate control description for the control plane and license authority, including signing-key custody, or document the self-registration and disconnected deployment modes as the path for organizations that cannot accept the dependency.

programGaps.title: Security documentation does not match the implementation in places
programGaps.description: compliance/ssp.md and docs/workspace-security-model.md describe the workspace sandbox as nono, while the code applies landstrip (Landlock and seccomp) through files still named workspace-nono; docs/security.md describes the current behavior.
programGaps.remediation: Update the SSP generator text and workspace documentation to name landstrip, and rename the files.
